name: Ploshchad Mira Museum Centre
known: Directors: Mikhail Shubsky 1991 to 2016, Maria Bukova 2016 to 2023, Olga Temnikova from 2023 (Russian Wikipedia).
Sergey Kovalevsky is artistic director and commissioner of the biennale (Sreda, V-A-C).
Founder: the Ministry of Culture of Krasnoyarsk Krai is the single founder of the institution, which is a regional state autonomous cultural institution (Rusprofile, from the state company register).
It belongs to the Russian national committee of ICOM; its founder and owner is the Krasnoyarsk Krai Ministry of Culture, a government body that is skipped.

name: AZ Museum (Anatoly Zverev Museum)
known: Natalia Opaleva is founder and general director, and Polina Lobachevskaya is co-organiser and art director (Vedomosti, Snob, Interfax).
Its one standing tie is the AZ/ART centre in the Maroseika chambers, founded by the same patron, Natalia Opaleva.
Press says its founder funds it from her own money.

name: Fabrika Centre for Creative Industries
known: Asya Filippova began work as General Director of the Oktyabr technical paper factory in 2003 and leads the centre (Fabrika's about page).

name: GES-2 House of Culture
known: Teresa Iarocci Mavica stepped down as GES-2 director weeks after the opening.

V-A-C's artistic director Francesco Manacorda resigned in March 2022 citing the war, and Ragnar Kjartansson pulled out of his planned opening project Santa Barbara (The Art Newspaper, Sophia Kishkovsky, 19 October 2022).
Alisa Prudnikova was appointed programme director of V-A-C and GES-2 in May 2022 (The Art Newspaper, 19 October 2022).
Mikhelson is chairman, CEO and major shareholder of the natural gas producer Novatek (Wikipedia);
The site names only the founder Leonid Mikhelson.
Francesco Manacorda resigned as artistic director Mar 2022.

name: Garage Museum
known: Daria Kotova, previously director of the endowment fund, replaced founding director Anton Belov in April 2025 (The Art Newspaper).
Garage is a project of the IRIS Foundation, founded by Zhukova (stated by the space); no reporting found of its annual budget or accounts.
A non-profit project of the IRIS Foundation, founded by Dasha Zhukova, which offers a joint master's programme with the Higher School of Economics.

name: Jewish Museum and Tolerance Center
known: Alexander Boroda is listed as director in Wikipedia's infobox and as president of the Federation of Jewish Communities of Russia in JTA.

In February 2014 the museum set up an endowment and raised $4.5 million in one evening at a gala dinner; co-founders of the fund were Viktor Vekselberg, Leonard Blavatnik, Roman Abramovich, Vadim Moshkovich, Alexey Likhtenfeld, Alexander Klyachin, Gennady Timchenko and Mikhail Gutseriev (Kommersant,

name: Moscow International Biennale of Contemporary Art
Moscow Museum of Modern Art (MMOMA)
known: Zurab Tsereteli's grandson Vasili Tsereteli became executive director in 2001 or 2002 (The Calvert Journal gives 2001, Snob gives 2002).

name: Multimedia Art Museum, Moscow (MAMM)
known: Founded by the Government of Moscow in 1996 as the Moscow House of Photography, the first Russian state art institution focused on photography.
The museum was founded by the Government of Moscow and is supported by the Moscow Department of Culture (MAMM website).

name: Museum of Contemporary History of Russia
Museum of Russian Impressionism
known: Founded by the collector Boris Mints (O1 Group).
Director: Yulia Petrova (Wikipedia;

Founder Boris Mints: The Art Newspaper (Sophia Kishkovsky, 28 June 2018) reported that news of his family's departure for London emerged at the end of May 2018, and that it was unclear whether he would keep funding the museum from the UK; director Petrova declined to discuss his ongoing support.

Since February 2024 the patron-trustee and head of the board of trustees is Vladimir Voronin, a businessman and shareholder of the FSK group of companies, which The Art Newspaper Russia (Sofia Bagdasarova, 15 February 2024) calls its founder and president (RTVI, 15 February 2024, calls him president
He said he considers it his duty to provide such support, and director Petrova said his role allows the museum to carry out a long-delayed modernisation of the building and equipment.
Director Petrova said about 40% of the budget comes from tickets, tours, classes, souvenirs and catalogues, and the rest from commercial partnerships and donations (The Art Newspaper Russia, 2024).

name: Pushkin State Museum of Fine Arts
known: Ekaterina Pronicheva was named director on 14 January 2026, announced by Culture Minister Olga Lyubimova.
Marina Loshak, director since 2013, resigned on 20 March 2023 (Moscow Times).
Board of trustees, chaired by Deputy Prime Minister Marat Khusnullin: Culture Minister Olga Lyubimova;
Pyotr Fradkov, chairman of Promsvyazbank;
Ekaterina Pronicheva is director now.

name: Ruarts Foundation
known: Art director is Catherine Borissoff (spelled Katrin Borisov in Russian press).
The Ruarts founder has the same name.
Founded by collector Marianna Sardarova, who also set up the separate RuArts Gallery; it states it works with state museums but names no standing partner.
Its About page names founder Marianna Sardarova and art director Catherine Borissoff.
